title: Algebraic Group Actions, Orbits, Stabilizers, and Controlled Quotients

items.title: Quotient sheaves and representable quotients for pre-relations and group actions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the sheafification and represented-sheaf suppliers used below. Work on a fixed big fppf site of $k$-schemes as in Stacks §34.7. Let $k$ be a field, and let $s,t:R\to U$ be two morphisms of $k$-schemes with common target ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]); such a pair is a **pre-relation** on $U$. The **naive quotient presheaf** $P_{U/R}$ is the functor on the category of $k$-schemes sending a $k$-scheme $T$ to the quotient of the set $U(T)$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]) by the equivalence relation generated by $\{(s(x),t(x)):x\in R(T)\}$; its value at $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the set of $k$-points of $U$ modulo the relation generated by $R(k)$. $P_{U/R}$ is in general only a presheaf ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]). An **fppf sheaf** on this category is a presheaf $F$ such that for every $k$-scheme $T$ and every fppf covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ — a set-indexed family of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation which is jointly surjective onto $T$ ([[def-faithfully-flat-morphism-schemes]], [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) — the diagram $F(T)\to\prod_iF(T_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(T_i\times_TT_j)$ is an equalizer. The **fppf quotient sheaf** $U/R$ is the sheafification of $P_{U/R}$ for this topology: a morphism $P_{U/R}\to U/R$ of presheaves with $U/R$ an fppf sheaf, initial among morphisms from $P_{U/R}$ to fppf sheaves. Every representable presheaf is an fppf sheaf ([[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]); a $k$-scheme $M$ **represents the quotient sheaf** $U/R$ when there is a natural isomorphism $h_M\cong U/R$ ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]), and then $M$ is unique up to unique isomorphism. For a group scheme $G$ of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) acting on $U$ one takes $R=G\times_kU$ with $s$ the second projection and $t$ the action morphism, and writes $U/G$; for $U=G$ and a closed subgroup scheme $H\subseteq G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]) acting by right translation one takes $R=G\times_kH$, $s(g,h)=g$, $t(g,h)=gh$, and writes $G/H$. The natural map from the naive quotient presheaf to its quotient sheaf is generally not an isomorphism; sheafification can both identify sections that agree locally and introduce sections that only have local representatives. The orbit set is only $P_{U/R}(k)$.
items.strategy: Definition record following Stacks Definition 39.20.1 (tag 02VG) and Definition 39.20.2 (tag 03BD), with the fppf topology of Stacks Section 34.7 (tags 021Q, 021R, 021S) and the sheaf condition of Stacks Section 7.7 (tag 00VM). The naive quotient is only a presheaf, so its sheafification must be defined; represented functors are fppf sheaves by the published descent lemma for scheme morphisms. No claim of representability is made in the definition. Covering families need not be finite globally. Over each affine target open, openness of the covering maps and quasi-compactness allow a finite affine refinement, exactly as in the proof of [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]. Sheafification is the two-step plus construction of Stacks Sites and Sheaves §7.10, Theorem 7.10.10, Definition 7.10.11 and Proposition 7.10.12. The naive presheaf definition itself uses no selection, but the published represented-sheaf supplier explicitly assumes AC.

items.title: Algebraic group actions, orbit maps, orbit subschemes and scheme-theoretic stabilizers
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$
([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) and let $X$ be a $k$-scheme
([[def-scheme-over-base]]). An **action** of $G$ on $X$ is a morphism
$\alpha:G\times_kX\to X$ ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]) such that the unit and
associativity diagrams commute:
$\alpha(e\times\operatorname{id}_X)=\operatorname{id}_X$ and
$\alpha(\operatorname{id}_G\times\alpha)=\alpha(m\times\operatorname{id}_X)$,
where $m$ is the multiplication of $G$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of $k$-schemes on
which $G$ acts is **equivariant** if
$f\alpha_X=\alpha_Y(\operatorname{id}_G\times f)$. The action is determined by
its values on $R$-points, giving an action of the abstract group $G(R)$ on
$X(R)$ for every $k$-algebra $R$.

For $x\in X(k)$ ([[lem-field-valued-points-of-schemes]]) the **orbit map** is
$\varrho_x:G\to X$, $\varrho_x(g)=\alpha(g,x)$; for separated finite-type $X$,
its image on $k$-points is the **rational orbit** $G(k)\cdot x$, whereas its
underlying topological image is $|\varrho_x|(|G|)\subseteq|X|$. The orbit set
$X(k)/G(k)$ is the set of all rational orbits. The **reduced orbit subscheme**
$O_x$ means this locally closed image with reduced structure, when local
closedness is established; the orbit lemma below constructs it for smooth $G$.
For a nonsmooth group, the orbit map need not factor through this reduced
subscheme: translation of $\alpha_p$ on $\mathbb A^1$ at $0$ has a one-point
reduced orbit but a nonconstant infinitesimal orbit map. A factorization
$G\to O_x$ must therefore be justified or explicitly assumed.

The **scheme-theoretic stabilizer** (isotropy group) is the fibre product
$G_x:=G\times_{X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ formed with $\varrho_x$ and the $k$-point
$x$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]],
[[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]): for separated finite-type
$X$ it is a closed subscheme of $G$, and for every $k$-algebra $R$ its
$R$-points are $G_x(R)=\{g\in G(R):\alpha(g,x_R)=x_R\}$. The pair
$R=G\times_kX\rightrightarrows X$ with $s(g,z)=z$ and $t(g,z)=\alpha(g,z)$ is
the **action groupoid** of the action, a pre-relation on $X$
([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]). When $X$ is separated and
of finite type over $k$, $k$-points are closed, so $G_x$ is a closed subgroup
scheme of $G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]).

The reduced orbit $O_x$ need not equal the scheme-theoretic image
([[def-scheme-theoretic-image]]): the latter is closed and is normally the orbit
closure, whereas the orbit is only locally closed. Fibres and the kernel pair of
$\varrho_x:G\to X$ are always defined; a kernel pair over $O_x$ requires a
factorization through the reduced orbit ([[def-locally-closed-immersion]]).
items.strategy: Definition record following Milne, Algebraic Groups (2022), Chapter 7 Sections 7(c)-(b), printed pp. 139-140 (orbit maps, isotropy groups defined as fibres of the orbit map, orbit subschemes), and Brion, Introduction to actions of algebraic groups, Definition 1.4 and Definition 1.10, printed pp. 3-5. The stabilizer is introduced as the fibre product so that it is a priori a scheme, not merely a subgroup of points; closedness of the fibre uses that a $k$-point of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme is a closed point. The action groupoid is recorded because the quotient sheaf of this page is the quotient of that pre-relation. Distinguish rational orbits, the topological orbit image and the quotient orbit set. The reduced orbit need not equal the scheme-theoretic image: the latter is closed and is normally the orbit closure, whereas the orbit is only locally closed. Fibers and the kernel pair of $\varrho_x:G\to X$ are always defined; a kernel pair over $O_x$ requires a factorization through the reduced orbit. Only the pre-relation terminology from the quotient definition is used here; the represented-sheaf consequence is not invoked. The action/stabilizer definitions therefore carry no choice assumption.

items.title: Criterion for a scheme to represent an fppf quotient sheaf
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the represented-sheaf and geometric suppliers used on this page. Let $k$ be a field, let $s,t:R\to U$ be a pre-relation on $k$-schemes with fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]), and let $q:U\to M$ be a morphism to a $k$-scheme $M$. Assume: (1) $q\circ s=q\circ t$; (2) $q$ induces a surjection of fppf sheaves $h_U\to h_M$ (for instance, $q$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation); (3) the morphism $(t,s):R\to U\times_MU$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]) induces a surjection of fppf sheaves $h_R\to h_{U\times_MU}$ (for instance $(t,s)$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation). Then $M$ represents the quotient sheaf $U/R$.
items.strategy: Apply Stacks Lemma 39.20.3, but spell out its injectivity step. A section of the quotient sheaf is locally represented by a section of $U$, by the plus-construction description of sheafification. Thus (2) gives local lifts of every $M$-section and makes $U/R\to h_M$ surjective. If two quotient sections have the same image, refine a covering until both are represented by $u,v\in U(T_i)$. Their common $M$-image defines a section of $U\times_MU$; (3) lifts it locally to $R$, making those local representatives equivalent. They therefore agree as quotient-sheaf sections. Sheaf separatedness glues this equality, proving injectivity. Condition (1) gives the factorization, and represented functors are fppf sheaves under the explicitly assumed AC through [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]. No false assertion that related points of $U$ are equal in $U$ is used.

items.title: Affine finite locally free equivalence relations have finite locally free scheme quotients
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $s,t:R\to U$ be finite locally free morphisms ([[def-faithfully-flat-morphism-schemes]]) such that $j=(t,s):R\to U\times_kU$ is an equivalence relation. Put $C=\{a\in A: s^\sharp(a)=t^\sharp(a)\}$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] for the quotient sheaf $U/R$). Then $C$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra, the morphism $U\to M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite locally free and surjective, the canonical morphism $R\to U\times_MU$ is an isomorphism, and $M$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$.
items.strategy: This is the affine finite-locally-free case of Stacks Proposition 39.23.9 (tag 03BM), recorded in the form used by this page and discharged by the published theorem [[thm-nonaffine-finite-flat-affine-equivalence-quotient]], which proves exactly this statement for affine finite-type schemes over a field: $C$ is finite type, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite locally free and onto, $R\cong U\times_MU$, and $M$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf. The only reconciliation is the notion of quotient sheaf: the published theorem's phrase 'represents the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$' is the notion defined in [[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] (sheafification of the naive quotient presheaf in the fppf topology), so no hypothesis is added and no step of the published proof is repeated. The source remains Stacks 39.23.9; the design's promise for this pair is covered by this recorded interface.

items.title: Fibres of the orbit map and the scheme-theoretic stabilizer as a closed subgroup scheme
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice only for the closed-point selection in the finite-field trivialization of a nonempty fiber. Let $G$ be any finite-type $k$-group scheme acting on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, and let $x\in X(k)$. (a) The scheme-theoretic stabilizer $H=G_x=G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a closed subgroup scheme, with $H(R)=\{g:gx_R=x_R\}$ for every $k$-algebra $R$. (b) The scheme fiber $F_y=G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $y\in X(k)$ is empty unless $y$ belongs to the underlying image of the orbit map. If $y=g_0x$ with $g_0\in G(k)$, then $F_y=g_0H$. In general, if $F_y$ is nonempty, it becomes such a translate after a finite field extension carrying a point of the fiber; it is an fppf right $H$-torsor, and need not have a $k$-point. For $g\in G(k)$, $G_{gx}=gHg^{-1}$. (c) The fiber over $(y,x)$ of $(g,z)\mapsto(gz,z):G\times X\to X\times X$ is canonically $F_y$. (d) The morphism $G\times H\to G\times_XG$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is an isomorphism. If $\varrho_x$ factors through a locally closed orbit subscheme $O_x\hookrightarrow X$, this is also the kernel pair over $O_x$, because an immersion is a monomorphism.
items.strategy: The rational point of separated $X$ is a closed immersion (a section of a separated morphism), so its pullback gives the closed stabilizer. The action axioms show its point functor is closed under identity, multiplication and inverse, and [[lem-closed-subgroup-scheme-valued-point-criterion]] supplies the subgroup scheme conclusion. Translation by $g_0$ gives the fiber and conjugacy identities when $g_0$ exists. A nonempty affine chart of the fiber has a maximal ideal by [[thm-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal-ideal]] under AC; its residue field is finite over $k$ by [[cor-field-finite-type-over-a-field-is-a-finite-extension]]; over that extension translation trivializes it as $H$. This extension is an fppf cover, so the fiber is an fppf torsor, without claiming a rational translate. For (c), fiber points force $z=x$ and $gx=y$. For (d), on every test algebra equal images $gx=g'x$ are equivalent to the unique relation $g^{-1}g'\in H(R)$; the inverse morphism is $(g,g')\mapsto(g,g^{-1}g')$. These explicit natural formulas prove a scheme isomorphism, including infinitesimal points. Finally equality in an immersion target is the same as equality in $X$, giving the kernel-pair assertion when the factorization exists.

items.title: A linear representation induces an action on projective space with the same line stabilizers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]]. Let $G$ be an affine finite-type $k$-group scheme, let $V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$ be the rational representation of [[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]. In the repository's quotient convention, $\mathbb P(V)$ represents invertible quotients of $V_T$ and has the natural action $g\cdot[q]=[q\circ r(g)^{-1}]$. Define the space of lines by $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V):=\mathbb P(V^\vee)$, using the dual representation $r^\vee(g)=(r(g)^{-1})^\vee$. Its $T$-points are equivalently rank-one locally direct summand subbundles $L\subseteq V_T$, with action $L\mapsto r(g)L$. A line $L\subseteq V$ gives the point $[L]$ via the rank-one quotient $V^\vee\twoheadrightarrow L^\vee$, not via $V\twoheadrightarrow V/L$. The scheme stabilizer of this point has $R$-points exactly $\{g:r(g)L_R=L_R\}$. Therefore any closed subgroup scheme with that line-stabilizer functor is $G_{[L]}$. No smoothness of $G$ or its subgroup is needed.
items.strategy: Use the exact rank-one quotient representability theorem on $V$ and $V^\vee$, with its stated AC. A quotient $V_T^\vee\to M$ dualizes to the locally split rank-one injection $M^\vee\to V_T$; conversely a line subbundle dualizes to a surjection, because its locally free quotient makes the sequence locally split. Duality gives the natural inverse bijections. For quotient points, $g\cdot(h\cdot q)=q r(h)^{-1}r(g)^{-1}=q r(gh)^{-1}$; inversion is anti-multiplicative, not multiplicative. On the dual representation this is exactly the action on line subbundles $L\mapsto r(g)L$. Naturality on every test scheme and Yoneda yield the action morphisms and the action axioms. The restriction quotient $V^\vee\to L^\vee$ is preserved as an isomorphism class exactly when its annihilator, and hence the double-annihilator line $L_T$, is preserved. This computes the scheme stabilizer on every algebra, rather than only over fields.

items.title: Smooth orbits are locally closed and their orbit maps are faithfully flat over every field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a smooth algebraic
group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) acting on
a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]), and let
$x\in X(k)$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]). Then the
orbit subscheme $O_x$ is locally closed in $X$ and stable under $G$, and the
orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite
presentation. In particular $O_x$ is smooth over $k$ and of finite type. The
Axiom of Choice is inherited from the named suppliers and is used to choose an
algebraic closure, field bases and closed points in the proof.
items.strategy: Follow Milne 1.65 and 7.4, filling the scheme and field-change steps. A finite-type group scheme over a field is separated: its rational identity is closed (in every affine neighborhood its residue field is $k$, hence its ideal is maximal), and its diagonal is the inverse image of the identity under $(g,h)\mapsto gh^{-1}$. Form the scheme-theoretic closure $Y$ of $\varrho_x:G\to X$ using [[thm-scheme-theoretic-image-quasi-compact-morphism]]. On an affine target chart the ideal is $\ker(A\to\prod_jB_j)$ for a finite affine cover of its inverse image, as in that supplier's proof. For every field extension $K/k$, flat tensor extension preserves this kernel and finite product, so $Y_K$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $G_K\to X_K$. The $B_j\otimes K$ are reduced because $G$ is smooth; thus $A_K/I_K$ injects into a product of reduced rings, and $Y$ is geometrically reduced. Over an algebraic closure $K$, cover the inverse image of each affine target chart by finitely many affine source charts. Their coordinate maps are finitely presented, since the target rings are Noetherian and the source rings have finite type. Apply [[lem-finite-presentation-image-constructible]] with $b=1$ to each chart, and take the finite union: the full scheme-point image is constructible, including nonclosed points. In a Noetherian space a dense constructible subset contains a dense open: write it as a finite union of locally closed subsets and, on each irreducible component away from the other components, one of these subsets is dense and contains an open. Thus the image contains a dense open of $Y_K$. Nonempty locally closed subsets have closed $K$-points by the Nullstellensatz, which will justify the uses of transitivity below. Each $g\in G(K)$ acts on $X_K$ by an automorphism preserving the orbit image and its scheme-theoretic closure $Y_K$, by equivariance and the universal property of the image. Translates of this open therefore lie in the image and cover every closed orbit point. Their union is open in $Y_K$; its constructible complement in the image is empty because a nonempty constructible subset of a finite-type $K$-scheme has a closed point. Thus the full scheme-theoretic underlying image, including nonclosed points, is open in $Y_K$. The orbit set is saturated under $|Y_K|\to|Y|$: nonempty fibers remain nonempty after field extension, since tensor products of field extensions over a common field are nonzero. This projection is surjective and closed: $K/k$ is algebraic, so it is an integral map on affine charts, and integral maps are closed: the image of a closed set $V(J)$ is $V(J\cap A)$ by [[thm-lying-over]] applied to the induced integral quotient ring map; a surjective closed map is a quotient map. Hence the image is open in $Y$, defining $O_x$ as this open reduced subscheme. The orbit map factors through it and formation of $O_x$ commutes with this algebraic-closure base change. The action preserves $O_x$ scheme-theoretically: after that field change, the product $G_K\times O_{x,K}$ is reduced: on reduced target charts inject their rings into the finite product of the fraction fields of their minimal-prime quotients, tensor with a source chart, and use geometric reducedness of $G_K$ over each field and its closed points map into $O_{x,K}$; functions defining the orbit closure pull back to zero, and the open-complement preimage is empty. Flat descent of vanishing gives the same factorization over $k$. For flatness over $K$, remove intersections of the finitely many irreducible components of $O_{x,K}$, apply [[thm-generic-flatness-morphisms]] separately on these Noetherian integral charts, and combine the resulting dense open subsets. Translate this open by $G(K)$ to cover every closed point of the homogeneous target; source translation and target action identify the orbit maps over these opens, so they are flat. The translates cover the whole finite-type scheme (a nonempty closed complement would have a closed point), making the orbit map flat and surjective over $K$. On affine charts [[thm-faithfully-flat-descent-of-flatness]] descends flatness to $k$, and surjectivity is already known. The morphism is locally of finite presentation because both schemes have finite type over a field and the rings are Noetherian. Finally $O_{x,K}$ is reduced and has a nonempty regular locus by [[thm-nonempty-regular-locus-reduced-variety-perfect-field]]; regularity equals smoothness over the perfect field $K$ by [[thm-regular-equals-smooth-over-perfect-field]]. The smooth locus is open and invariant under the transitive action, so it is all of $O_{x,K}$. Geometric regularity descends under field extension by [[lem-ag-geometric-regularity-field-tests]], proving smoothness of $O_x/k$. This argument needs neither connectedness of $G$ nor smoothness of its scheme stabilizer. AC also supplies an algebraic closure, field bases and closed-point selections; all consumer applicability hypotheses are unchanged.

items.title: A faithfully flat orbit map represents the coset quotient sheaf
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the represented-sheaf and geometric suppliers used on this page. Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ acting on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]), let $x\in X(k)$, and let $H$ be a closed subgroup scheme of $G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]) with $H=G_x$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]). Assume the orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, where $O_x$ is the orbit subscheme. Then $O_x$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]), the quotient morphism is $\varrho_x$, and the kernel-pair morphism $G\times_kH\to G\times_{O_x}G$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Apply the representability criterion (Stacks 39.20.3) to the pre-relation $R=G\times_kH\rightrightarrows U=G$ with $s(g,h)=g$, $t(g,h)=gh$, and $q=\varrho_x:U\to O_x$. Condition (1) holds because $H=G_x$ fixes $x$, so $\varrho_x(gh)=(gh)x=gx=\varrho_x(g)$. Condition (2) holds by the faithful flatness and finite presentation of $\varrho_x$. Condition (3) is the kernel-pair isomorphism supplied for the orbit by the fibre computation of the orbit-map lemma, transported along the identification $H=G_x$: on $R$-points, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ is a bijection onto the pairs of $G(R)$ with equal image in $O_x(R)$. This is Milne's proof of Proposition 7.11, with the quotient sheaf formulation of Stacks 39.20.

items.title: Fibre dimension and orbit dimension add to the dimension of the group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a connected smooth algebraic group scheme of finite type over $k$ (such a $G$ is separated by Milne 1.22 and geometrically reduced, hence a classical variety of finite type over $k$) acting on a classical variety $X$ over $k$ ([[def-dimension-classical-variety]], [[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), and let $x\in X(k)$ be a closed point. Then: (a) every fibre over a closed $k$-point of the orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is a left translate of the stabilizer $G_x$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]), hence has underlying topological dimension $\dim G_x$, equivalently the dimension of its reduction; $G_x$ may be nonreduced ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); (b) $\dim G=\dim G_x+\dim O_x$; (c) the orbit closure $\overline{O_x}$ is the union of $O_x$ and of orbits of strictly smaller dimension; consequently every orbit of minimal dimension in $X$ is closed, and $\overline{O_x}$ contains a closed orbit. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the generic-fibre and constructibility inputs.
items.strategy: By [[lem-nonaffine-connected-group-geometrically-connected]], the smooth connected group $G$ is integral over the algebraically closed field, so its orbit and closure are irreducible. The orbit lemma makes $O_x$ a smooth locally closed classical variety. A nonempty fiber over a closed $k$-point has a $k$-point by the weak Nullstellensatz, so [[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]] gives an actual scheme translate of $G_x$; take reductions when applying classical dimension suppliers. Apply [[thm-generic-fibre-dimension]] to the dominant map between the irreducible classical varieties $G\to O_x$: on the supplied nonempty open its reduced fibers have dimension $\dim G-\dim O_x$, while all these closed-point fibers are translates of the same reduced stabilizer. Thus $\dim G=\dim G_x+\dim O_x$ even when $G_x$ is nonsmooth. The orbit is open in its irreducible closure. Its boundary is a proper closed subset, invariant under all $G(k)$ automorphisms; every boundary orbit has closure in that boundary and strictly smaller dimension by [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]]. This proves the strict-dimension closure statement. Repeatedly pass to a boundary orbit if the orbit is not closed; dimensions strictly decrease in the nonnegative integers, so the process terminates at a closed orbit. No infinite choice is required. The AC hypothesis is inherited from the exact geometric, dimension and Nullstellensatz suppliers. Here fibres in (a) are closed-point fibres, exactly as in the classical dimension supplier; a fibre over an arbitrary scheme point is instead a torsor over its residue field and is a translate only after a field extension providing a point. No translate by an element of $G(k)$ is asserted for such a fibre.

items.title: Homogeneous spaces of smooth affine groups are separated schemes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) and let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is representable by a separated $k$-scheme of finite type, unique up to unique isomorphism, and the quotient morphism $G\to G/H$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation. Moreover there are a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, a rational representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$ ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]) and a line $L\subseteq V$ with scheme-theoretic line stabilizer $H$, such that $G/H$ is isomorphic to the orbit $O_{[L]}$ of $[L]$ under the induced action on $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)=\mathbb P(V^\vee)$ ([[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]]) and the resulting morphism $G/H\to\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ is an immersion ([[def-locally-closed-immersion]]). In particular $G/H$ is separated and finite type over $k$, and no smoothness of $H$ is required. The Axiom of Choice is used through the generic-flatness, constructibility and Chevalley inputs cited in the proof.
items.strategy: This is Milne, Theorem 7.18, printed p. 143, with Proposition 7.17, printed p. 143. Step 1: Chevalley's theorem, in the published local form [[lem-nonaffine-subgroup-scheme-stabilizer-of-line]], supplies a finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ and a line $L\subseteq V$ whose scheme-theoretic stabilizer is exactly $H$; no smoothness of $H$ or of the representation is used. Step 2: by [[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]] the representation induces an action of $G$ on $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)=\mathbb P(V^\vee)$ (a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, by the published closed-diagonal lemma for relative projective space) such that the scheme-theoretic stabilizer of the point $[L]$ is $H$. Step 3: take $x=[L]$ and $O_x\subseteq\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ its orbit subscheme. Since $G$ is smooth, [[lem-orbit-map-faithfully-flat-and-orbit-locally-closed]] applies over the given field: $O_x$ is locally closed and smooth, and $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation. In particular the hypotheses of Step 4 hold. Step 4: [[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]] shows that $O_x$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ with quotient morphism $\varrho_x$. Step 5: $O_x$ is a locally closed subscheme of the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$, so it is separated and finite type over $k$ by the published stability of separatedness under immersions; uniqueness of the representing object is Yoneda. The AC use is exactly that of the generic-flatness and constructibility inputs in Step 3 and of the Chevalley input in Step 1. The subgroup supplier supplies a line in $V$, so its point is the restriction quotient $V^\vee\to L^\vee$; this explicitly reconciles Milne's line convention with the repository's quotient projective bundle convention. Every finite-type group and the representation used here satisfy the affine hypotheses of the representation definition.

items.title: Orbit sets, fppf quotient sheaves and representing schemes are three different objects
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the represented-sheaf and geometric suppliers used on this page. Three objects are commonly conflated, and must be kept apart. (1) The **orbit set** $U(k)/R(k)$: the value at $k$ of the naive quotient presheaf of a pre-relation; it is computed from $k$-points alone. (2) The **fppf quotient sheaf** $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]): the sheafification of that presheaf, whose sections over a $k$-scheme $T$ are fppf-local orbit data. Its $k$-points can be strictly larger than the orbit set, and it carries infinitesimal information invisible to it; a concrete instance is recorded on the examples companion page of this pair. (3) A **representing scheme**: a $k$-scheme $M$ with a natural isomorphism $h_M\cong U/R$ ([[lem-fppf-quotient-representability-criterion]]); by Yoneda it is unique up to unique isomorphism when it exists. Representability is an additional property, not a consequence of the definitions: this page establishes it for homogeneous spaces of smooth affine groups ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]]) and for affine finite locally free equivalence relations ([[thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-locally-free-equivalence-relation]]). In the homogeneous-space case the quotient is the orbit of the base point and the quotient morphism is faithfully flat ([[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]]); the general arbitrary-group quotient representability statement is outside the scope of this page and is not claimed here.
items.strategy: Remark separating the three notions, following Stacks Definition 39.20.1 and Section 66.14 and Milne, Chapter 5 Section 5(c) and Chapter 7 Section 7(e). The distinction between the orbit set and the quotient sheaf is made precise by the orbit-set counterexample on the examples companion page; the distinction between a quotient sheaf and a representing scheme is exactly the gap between Definition 39.20.1 and the representability statements proved here. The remark deliberately claims representability only in the two cases proved, matching the design's source gate on general arbitrary-group quotients.

items.title: The orbit set of k-points need not be the k-points of the fppf quotient sheaf
items.statement:
For every finite-type $k$-group scheme $G$ acting on a finite-type $k$-scheme
$X$, the orbit set $X(k)/G(k)$ of $k$-points computes the $k$-points of the
fppf quotient sheaf $X/G$.
items.strategy: Standard Galois-descent computation, structured as a counterexample to the statement that the naive quotient presheaf computes the fppf quotient. Setup: because $a$ is a nonsquare and $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, $x^2-a$ is irreducible and separable, so $k[x]/(x^2-a)$ is a separable quadratic field extension $K/k$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite étale of degree $2$ over $k$: the algebra is free of rank $2$ and finitely presented over $k$, and $\Omega_{A/k}=A\,dx/(2x\,dx)=0$ because $x$ (and hence $2x$) is a unit in $A$, so the published equivalence flat + unramified + finitely presented = étale applies. A $k$-algebra map $k[x]/(x^2-a)\to k$ would send $x$ to a square root of $a$, so $X(k)=\emptyset$. The cited isomorphism: in $k[x,y]/(x^2-a,y^2-a)$ one has $x^2=y^2=a\in k^\times$, so $x$ and $y$ are units; the displayed map has the explicit inverse sending $x$ in the target to $y$ in the source and $t$ to $x/y$; these are well defined because both source variables square to the unit $a$. The two composites fix each generator, giving an isomorphism. Then $j=(t,s)$ is an isomorphism, $s=\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $t$ are finite locally free of rank $2$, and the published affine quotient theorem applies with invariants $C=\{f: s^\sharp(f)=t^\sharp(f)\}=k$ (a general element $\alpha+\beta x$ satisfies $t^\sharp(f)=s^\sharp(f)$ only when $\beta=0$, since $x$ is a unit and $t-1\ne0$ in $k[t,x]/(t^2-1,x^2-a)$); hence $X/G$ is represented by $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Failure of the sheaf property: over the fppf cover $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the class of the identity section is a compatible family of sections of the presheaf that does not descend, since $X(k)/G(k)=\emptyset$; this exhibits the difference between the naive orbit set and the quotient sheaf. Note that the quotient sheaf here is representable: the counterexample separates the orbit set from the quotient sheaf, not representability from the quotient sheaf.

items.title: The quotient of GL2 by the diagonal torus is the complement of the diagonal in P1 x P1
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the homogeneous-space and
projective-bundle suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2$ with its
standard representation on $V=k^2$
([[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]]), and let
$T\subseteq G$ be the diagonal torus, the closed subgroup scheme whose
$R$-points are the invertible diagonal matrices
([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]],
[[lem-closed-subgroup-scheme-valued-point-criterion]]). (a) $T$ is a closed
subgroup scheme of the smooth affine group scheme $G$, and the fppf quotient
sheaf $G/T$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is
representable ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]]). (b) Let $G$
act on $Y=\mathbb P^1_k\times_k\mathbb P^1_k$ by the product of the actions
induced on each factor by the standard representation
([[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]]), and let
$o=(\langle e_1\rangle,\langle e_2\rangle)\in Y(k)$. Then the stabilizer of $o$
is $T$, the orbit $O_o$ is exactly the open subscheme
$\{(L_1,L_2)\in Y: L_1\ne L_2\}$ (complement of the diagonal), and the orbit
map induces an isomorphism $G/T\cong O_o$
([[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]],
[[lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dimension]]). (c) Consequently $G/T$ is
a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme whose base change to an algebraic
closure has dimension $2$ (equal to $\dim G-\dim T=4-2$, by the
orbit-stabilizer dimension identity); the morphism $G/T\to\mathbb P^1_k$,
$(L_1,L_2)\mapsto L_1$, has over every point $y\in\mathbb P^1_k$ a fibre
isomorphic to $\mathbb P^1_{\kappa(y)}$ minus the $\kappa(y)$-rational point
defined by $y$; and for every extension field $K/k$ the natural map
$G(K)/T(K)\to(G/T)(K)$ is a bijection.
items.strategy: Milne, Example 7.19 and Theorem 7.18, printed p. 143, computes the quotient of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ by a line stabilizer; here the subgroup is the diagonal torus rather than the Borel, and the orbit is taken on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. (a) The diagonal matrices form a closed subgroup scheme: they are cut out by the vanishing of the two off-diagonal coordinates, and the valued-point criterion identifies the closed subscheme they define with the functor $R\mapsto\{(R^\times)^2\}$; smoothness and affineness of $G$ are those of the published $\mathrm{GL}_2$ item. (b) Use $\mathbb P(V^\vee)$ on each factor, as in the repaired projective-action lemma, to parametrize lines in $V$. For $V=k^2$ each is $\mathbb P^1_k$ and the action is $L\mapsto gL$; the action on the product is the diagonal action. A matrix stabilizes the ordered pair $(\langle e_1\rangle,\langle e_2\rangle)$ exactly when it preserves both coordinate lines, i.e. is diagonal with unit entries. Transitivity on pairs of distinct lines: given distinct lines $L_1,L_2$ over any field $K$, choose nonzero $u\in L_1$, $v\in L_2$; they form a basis, and the matrix with columns $u,v$ lies in $G(K)$ and moves the standard pair to $(L_1,L_2)$. The pointwise calculation identifies the geometric orbit set with the complement of the diagonal. To identify the scheme and the quotient over every base, a pair of line subbundles in this complement has invertible wedge determinant, so their direct sum is $V_T$. On a Zariski cover choose frames for both line bundles; the two frame columns give an invertible matrix. These lifts prove that $G\to Y\setminus\Delta$ is locally a product with $T=\mathbf G_m^2$, hence is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, with the stated kernel pair. The representability criterion therefore gives $G/T\cong Y\setminus\Delta$ as schemes, not just on field-valued points; that complement is open because $Y$ is separated and the diagonal is a closed immersion. Since $G$ is smooth, the orbit map onto $O_o$ is faithfully flat of finite type, and the coset-quotient proposition identifies $G/T$ with $O_o$. (c) Smoothness and separatedness of $G/T$ follow from the locally closed smooth orbit and the open immersion into the separated scheme $Y$. For the dimension: after base change to an algebraic closure $\bar k$, the orbit-stabilizer dimension identity gives $\dim_{\bar k}(G/T)_{\bar k}=\dim G_{\bar k}-\dim T_{\bar k}=4-2=2$, using $\dim\mathrm{GL}_2=4$ (open in the fourfold affine space) and $\dim T=2$ ($T\cong\mathbf G_m^2$); dimension of a finite-type $k$-scheme is unchanged by passing to an algebraic closure. The fibres of the first projection over $L_1$ are the complement of the point $L_1$ in $\mathbb P^1$, and $K$-rational points of $O_o$ are the pairs of distinct $K$-rational lines, in bijection with $G(K)/T(K)$ by transitivity and the stabilizer computation. Over any scheme point y of the first P1_k, the fibre is P1_{kappa(y)} minus the canonical kappa(y)-rational point, including y generic.
